prerequisites: Principle of planning and control in robotic spaces (Joint, operational)

learning_outcomes.text: Implement visual servoing techniques based on 2D and 3D approaches in robotics, using camera data to control the movements of robotic manipulators, demonstrating their ability to ensure precision and stability in dynamic environments.
Understand the fundamental principles of visual servoing in robotics, including 2D and 3D approaches.
Identify the differences between position visual servoing (PBVS) and image visual servoing (IBVS) techniques, and understand their impact on robotic performance.
Acquire notions of interaction model (Jacobian interaction) between image space and real space (3D): case study of a point.
Know how to implement visual servoing algorithms, from existing libraries, in simulation environments.
Carry out tests to validate visual servoing algorithms and evaluate their effectiveness in tracking trajectories or manipulating objects.
Integrate vision sensors into a robotic system and use them for dynamic robot control applications.
Be aware of the issues related to the use of visual servoing in industrial environments, particularly in terms of precision, safety and robustness.
Develop a critical attitude and reflection on the methodological and technological choices in the design of vision-based control systems.
Be aware of the practical implications of technical decisions for the stability and performance of robotic systems in dynamic environments.

syllabus_topics: General introduction course
Overview of the learning and course objectives
Presentation of Problem-Based Learning (PBL)
Introduction to the principles of vision-based control and its applications in robotics
PBL 1: Introduction to visual servoing
Fundamental principles of visual servoing: definitions and key concepts
Differences between image servoing (IBVS) and position servoing (PBVS)
Possible configurations of vision systems for visual servoing
PBL 2: 3D visual servoing techniques
3D visual servoing approaches: principles and integration of spatial coordinates
Trajectory tracking based on 3D visual servoing: design and implementation
Example of formalization of an interaction matrix (image-3D relationship) of a point
PBL 3: 2D visual servoing techniques
Visual servoing based on 2D features: principles and algorithms
Implementation of 2D visual servoing for trajectory tracking
Analysis of the limits and performances of 2D approaches
Comparison of the performances of 3D techniques compared to 2D approaches: precision, robustness and applications
Restructuration course
Overall synthesis of APPs and concepts covered
Discussions and answers to questions raised during the APPs feedback phases
Assessment of targeted learning outcomes (AAVs) and prospects for professional applications
PT n°1: Implementation of 3D visual servoing
Use of Matlab/Simulink to program a 3D visual servoing (Toolbox by P. Corke)
4-point tracking test (square as a feature)
Tests of different starting points, different feature sizes,
PT n°2: Implementation of 2D visual servoing
Using Matlab/Simulink to program a 2D visual servoing (Toolbox by P. Corke)
Testing a program in the form of a block diagram (Simulink)
Testing different configurations of the 2D visual servoing (different starts, feature size, etc.)
Testing the robustness of the 2D visual servoing: Bad initialization of depth, loss of vision, etc.
teaching_methods: Small group sessions tutored by a teacher
bibliography: Peter I. Corke. 1997. Visual Control of Robots: High-Performance Visual Serving. John Wiley & Sons, Inc., USA.
